4. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The colors of Mardi Gras are purple, green, and gold, symbolizing justice, faith, and power, respectively.
5. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The first Mardi Gras parade in New Orleans took place in 1837.
6. [ASSISTANT_SAID] There are more than 70 parades in New Orleans during the Mardi Gras season.
7. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mardi Gras parade floats are often designed around a theme, and riders throw "throws" to the crowds, including beads, doubloons, and other trinkets.
8. [ASSISTANT_SAID] A famous Mardi Gras tradition is the wearing of masks, dating back to early celebrations in medieval Europe.
9. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The official Mardi Gras colors and flag were designed in 1872 by a group called the Rex organization.
10. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mardi Gras is celebrated in many parts of the world, including Brazil (known as Carnival) and Venice, Italy (known for its elaborate masquerade balls).
11. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The day after Mardi Gras is Ash Wednesday, marking the beginning of the Christian season of Lent, lasting for 40 days leading up to Easter.
12. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mardi Gras celebrations have been affected by historic events, including World War I, the Spanish flu pandemic, and Hurricane Katrina in 2005, but the spirit of the festival has always endured.
